commits.subject: Start the macOS accessibility helper as a utility process, not Ember's binary in node mode
Answer SSH's password prompts on macOS through Ember itself, not its binary in node mode
Turn node mode off in the macOS build, and prove in CI that Ember.app refuses it
Say in main.ts and the build script how the macOS accessibility host now starts

items.how: I checked the code first. On macOS only two helpers ran Ember's binary in node mode: the accessibility host and SSH askpass. The SSH link worker is a worker_thread, macOS commands run without the job host, and the Copilot runtime is its own binary. (1) Accessibility host: macOS now starts it with Electron's utilityProcess.fork (serviceName "Ember accessibility", stdio "pipe", its environment). A utility process has no stdin, so each JSON-RPC request goes as one message on Electron's parent port. Answers still come on stdout and notes on stderr, so the protocol and its lines are unchanged. The host also exits if its parent changes (Ember is gone), which is what stdin closing did before. AtspiSidecar now drives either kind of child behind one interface. If a kill is asked for before the child has spawned, it is sent once it spawns. A fork that throws fails the request and says why. hostLaunch on macOS drops ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (in any letter case) and throws for a packaged launch with no fork (fail closed). main.ts passes Electron's utilityProcess to the platform through ElectronParts. Windows is unchanged: its RunAsNode stays on for the commands job host, so moving the host alone gains nothing there, and its UI Automation bridge's process tree would need its own CI proof. (2) Askpass: the macOS wrapper now runs `unset ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`, then `EMBER_ASKPASS_PROMPT="$*"`, then `exec <Ember> [<dev tree>] --ember-askpass`. The prompt is never on Ember's command line, where Chromium or AppKit could read a server's text as a switch. main.ts handles this run first thing: askpassInEmber starts askpass.cjs as a worker thread, which uses the same socket, nonce and lines as on Linux. The worker writes the answer to fd 1 and stores the outcome in shared memory. The main thread waits blocked (Atomics.wait), so Electron never reaches its run loop: no single-instance lock, no window, nothing in the data folder, no Dock icon, and setActivationPolicy("prohibited") as well. app.exit then ends the process at once, with askpass.cjs's exit codes. A worker that never starts (15 s) or stops beating (10 s) counts as cancelled (exit 1). A user who takes minutes to answer is still waited for. No fallback was needed. Linux keeps its node-mode wrapper and Windows its compiled helper. (3) fuses.mjs: emberFuses(os) turns RunAsNode off for macOS only; Linux and Windows keep it on, and the reason is written in fuses.mjs. EMBER_FUSES is now the fuses for the running OS, so stage.mjs needed no code change. In ci.yml, jobs macos and macos-x64 no longer run the binary as plain Node. They now prove it is refused: given ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, a script and --inspect, the binary must start as Ember (its "doesn't start with debugging switches" message, exit 2), and the script's mark file must not exist. The NODE_OPTIONS check moves onto the --inspect run. The DYLD probe, still run only where SIP is on, now starts the app the same way and expects exit 2. Linux's and Windows' checks are unchanged. layout.mjs needed only a comment; mac-bundle.mjs's entitlement comment now names the utility processes. (4) ember-darwin's packaged host check now uses the packaged check-up's "Accessibility helper" row, since node mode is gone. New test/integration/askpass-darwin.test.ts, with its own step in the macos job.

problems.what: askpass-darwin samples LaunchServices (lsappinfo) only inside the askpass server's handler. The handler runs only after the worker has connected, which is long after main.ts called setActivationPolicy("prohibited"). If AppKit registers Ember as a Foreground app (a Dock tile) when NSApplication starts, before main.cjs runs, and "prohibited" then removes it, every SSH password prompt would flash a Dock icon and the test would never see it. The decision asks for no Dock icon before anything shows. This can only be checked on a real Mac, and the current sampling leaves it open.
problems.fix: In unlock(), start a 50 ms setInterval when ssh-add is spawned, stop it on ssh-add's exit, and push launchServicesType(pid) for every askpassPids() pid into `seen`. Keep `expect(r.seen).not.toContain("Foreground")`. That covers the askpass process's whole life, not only the time after it has connected.

verify.notes:
Verdict on F-177: the decision is built as written. What the agent narrowed is justified.
- Windows and Linux keep RunAsNode, as the lead scoped it, and fuses.mjs says why.
- Requests reach the host as parent-port messages instead of stdin because Electron utility processes have no stdin. The protocol lines themselves are unchanged.
- setActivationPolicy("prohibited") is used instead of "accessory", and the run loop is never reached. That is the same or stricter.
- No fallback was needed.
- The macOS askpass proof went into ci.yml (askpass-darwin) instead of remote.yml. remote.yml's ssh-macos job uses key auth with BatchMode and never exercised askpass, so this is a better proof.

What I confirmed in the code:
- No macOS launch with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE remains. The other places that set it are Windows only (connections.ts job host, local.ts WSL and win32, wsl/*) or Linux only (desk/agent.ts; darwin's desk is null). The Copilot runtime on macOS is a native binary (copilot-runtime), so the SDK's spawn of a .js file with process.execPath is never taken.
- hostLaunch on darwin drops ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE whatever its letter case. A packaged launch with no fork throws, so it fails closed. main.ts always passes Electron's utilityProcess. Electron 44's ForkOptions.disclaim defaults to false, so macOS still holds Ember responsible for the host. The voice utility process already loads native modules the same way.
- The host's pid is in Ember's own pids for commands (getAppMetrics and sidecar.pid).
- Windows' hostLaunch output and Linux's Python and askpass paths are byte-for-byte as before.
- The askpass mode does only one thing. The script path is fixed (__dirname/askpass.cjs). The nonce is checked against a regex, and the prompt is cut to 2048 characters. It asks one question and exits 0 or 1. The prompt never reaches the command line. It runs before the debug-switch check, but the main thread blocks before PreMainMessageLoopRun, so no DevTools server starts. A worker that crashes, never starts or stops beating ends in exit 1.

items.how:
On macOS only two helpers ran Ember's binary in node mode: the accessibility host and SSH askpass. The SSH link worker is a worker_thread, macOS commands run without the job host, and the Copilot runtime is its own binary.

(1) Accessibility host. macOS now starts it with Electron's utilityProcess.fork (serviceName "Ember accessibility", stdio "pipe", its own environment). A utility process has no stdin, so each JSON-RPC request goes as one message on the parent port. Answers still come on stdout and notes on stderr, so the protocol and its lines are unchanged. The host exits when its parent changes (Ember is gone), which is what stdin closing did before. AtspiSidecar drives either kind of child behind one interface. A kill asked for before spawn is sent once the child spawns. A fork that throws fails the request and says why. hostLaunch on macOS drops ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (in any letter case), and a packaged launch with no fork throws (fail closed). main.ts passes Electron's utilityProcess to the platform through ElectronParts. Windows is unchanged: its RunAsNode stays on for the commands job host, so moving the host alone gains nothing there.

(2) Askpass. The macOS wrapper is now `unset ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE; EMBER_ASKPASS_PROMPT="$*"; export; exec <Ember> [<dev tree>] --ember-askpass`. The prompt is never on the command line. main.ts handles this run first thing: it calls setActivationPolicy("prohibited"), then askpassInEmber runs askpass.cjs as a worker thread (same socket, nonce and lines as on Linux). The main thread blocks in Atomics.wait, so Electron never reaches its run loop: no lock, no window, no data-folder writes. app.exit then gives askpass.cjs's exit codes. A worker that never starts (15 s) or stops beating (10 s) counts as cancelled (exit 1). No fallback was needed. Linux keeps its node-mode wrapper and Windows its compiled helper.

(3) Packaging and CI. emberFuses(os) turns RunAsNode off for macOS only, and fuses.mjs gives the reason. EMBER_FUSES follows the running OS. In ci.yml's macos and macos-x64 packaged checks, Ember's binary is given ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, a script and --inspect. It must start as Ember ("doesn't start with debugging switches", exit 2), and the script's mark file must not exist. The DYLD probe (only where SIP is on) also expects exit 2.

NODE_OPTIONS on macOS (this pass corrects round 1). b73a59c's body said "the NODE_OPTIONS check moves onto the --inspect run", and that was wrong. A packaged Electron drops all but two NODE_OPTIONS in app mode whatever the fuse says, so that run can't fail. The comment above it now says `fuses.mjs --check` (EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable off) is the proof, and the run only shows --inspect is still refused with it set. The step names now say "NODE_OPTIONS fuse off". Linux and Windows steps are unchanged.

(4) Tests. ember-darwin's packaged host check reads the packaged check-up's "Accessibility helper" row. The new askpass-darwin suite has its own step in the macos job. Its sampler now runs every 50 ms from ssh-add's spawn to its exit, covering the askpass process's whole life. Each sample records how many askpass processes there are, what LaunchServices calls each, and their child processes (`pgrep -P`). The suite asserts: never Foreground, one askpass process, and children equal to [] ("the askpass run started no helper processes"). The cancel case checks the same three.

Keeping it is justified: activating Ember would make Ember the active app, which goes against the design and against M2's assertion that the user's app stays active while the box is up.
